summary: Announcement-stage project; no statutory consultation for a data-centre application has occurred. The developers commissioned a poll (True North Advisors / Diffley Partnership) reporting 62% of 1,303 people across Aberdeen and Aberdeenshire in favour of a 'green data centre, industrial and energy park' at Blackdog. Organised local scrutiny is now represented by AI Data Centres Awareness Group – Blackdog, Balmedie and surrounding area, a signatory to the August 2026 community-campaign coalition letter. APRS has added Blackdog to its data-centres campaign map and questions whether offshore wind should power data centres. Regional economic development bodies ONE and ETZ Ltd publicly support the project.

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: Around 1,000 construction jobs, ~100 permanent high-skilled roles, up to 2,000 indirect jobs, billions of pounds of private investment and a 'just transition' route for oil and gas workers

stakeholder_positions.position: Critical scrutiny: highlights that only a 2016 mixed-use PPiP exists, that detailed planning is yet to be submitted, that the site adjoins a dune system and a toxic oil-and-gas waste dump, and questions whether Scotland's offshore wind should be used for data centres.
Supportive: CEO Jennifer Craw says the north east's access to offshore wind gives it a competitive edge for hyperscale AI investment.
Supportive of the project as part of regional energy transition and digital economy ambitions.

Supportive as prospective power supplier: 'clean power enabling digital growth, and digital demand accelerating renewable deployment' (Laura Jarvie), while noting Aspen will first supply the grid and decarbonise oil and gas platforms.

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: AI Data Centres Awareness Group – Blackdog, Balmedie and surrounding area
stakeholder_positions.position: Signed the community-campaign coalition letter seeking a moratorium on hyperscale AI data-centre decisions pending national safeguards.

campaign_groups: AI Data Centres Awareness Group – Blackdog, Balmedie and surrounding area
notes: The 62%-in-favour poll was commissioned in connection with the developers' announcement and reported in their press release; the questionnaire and methodology have not been published, so it is recorded as a developer claim. The coalition letter establishes the local awareness group's participation but does not provide a project-specific objection count. Belhelvie Community Council covers the Blackdog area and has commented on other local applications; its position on the data centre was not located.
